Peak quiet corners rules
New handlers should know how a new handler works

This page covers the Companion Animal Travel Desk and why careful handling matters on every itinerary. Your job is to keep the process calm, clear, and safe for the traveler and the animal. Safety takes priority over speed, because rushed checks create avoidable errors.

When you receive a booking request, confirm the traveler details, the animal details, and the travel conditions before you move forward. Keep your language plain. State what you need, record what you learn, and do not improvise. If a record is incomplete, pause and route it through the proper review path instead of guessing. A safety coordinator reviews hazards and prevention, and you should treat that review as part of the standard process, not an extra step.

For booking, follow the required form and enter only accurate information. <<FACT F085>> Check that the form matches the passenger record and the animal record before any confirmation is issued. If the traveler changes the plan, update the file immediately so later staff do not work from stale notes.

During boarding preparation, keep the traveler informed and watch for signs that the animal is unsettled. Use steady, respectful phrasing. If a concern appears, separate the issue from the emotion and handle the facts first. <<FACT F093>> Escalation must stay orderly, with the correct desk support used at once when the situation exceeds routine handling. <<FACT F105>> Do not delay escalation while you continue casual conversation or try to solve a safety issue alone.

Before handoff, review containment, identification, and any special handling notes one last time. If a traveler asks for reassurance, give it in simple terms and avoid promises you cannot verify. If you are unsure, ask the senior coordinator rather than filling gaps from memory.

Remember to verify, record, and escalate without hesitation.
